## Toolkit

- **P2 — Runtime defect: recursive sizing adds cubic decoding work.** [marshal.go:1130](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal.go:1130) recursively classifies each remaining subtype, then repeats that classification while recursively calculating its minimum. Classification costs Θ(d), minimum calculation Θ(d²), and decoding nested singleton vectors Θ(d³), versus Θ(d²) at base. A depth-1,000 type fits wire metadata and requires only a four-byte float payload, yet adds approximately 167 million classification visits per decoded row. This work runs synchronously in `Scan`.

- **P2 — Runtime defect: previously supported empty nested vectors are rejected.** [marshal.go:1142](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal.go:1142) assigns a one-byte minimum to `vector<float,0>`, although its fixed-length encoding occupies zero bytes. For `vector<vector<float,0>,2>`, a non-NULL empty payload and `[][]float32` destination succeed at base but fail the new outer bound. Both pinned metadata parsers admit zero dimensions, and the exported zero-dimension API remains explicitly supported by tests.

## Standards

- **P3 — Factual documentation defect: the comment attributes eight bytes to each inner vector.** [marshal_vector_test.go:772](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal_vector_test.go:772) describes one outer length vint plus three zero-length text vints. That is **four bytes per inner vector**; eight bytes is the total for both elements. The aggregate assertion is correct.

- **P3 — Factual documentation defect: the documented byte minima exclude supported zero-byte encodings.** [marshal_vector_test.go:693](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal_vector_test.go:693) says an N-element vector never occupies fewer than N bytes; line 813 likewise denies a zero-byte element encoding. An outer vector containing N zero-dimensional fixed-element vectors occupies **zero bytes**. The helper’s “fewest bytes” description at [marshal.go:1121](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal.go:1121) and the first commit’s universal one-byte claim repeat this incorrect premise.

- **P3 — Factual documentation defect: array destinations contradict the universal allocation claim.** [marshal.go:986](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal.go:986) says every path below converts Dimensions into an allocation. The array branch uses existing storage and skips `reflect.MakeSlice`; the added array test correctly describes that behavior.

- **P3 — Repository-rule violation: both commits fail the prescribed message format.** Commits `0276a669` and `78891dd` start with lowercase `fix(marshal):` and omit the prescribed `Patch by …; reviewed by … for #####` trailer. [CONTRIBUTING.md:23](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/CONTRIBUTING.md:23) makes the format applicable to submitted patches; lines 37 and 42 specify these requirements. Both commits contain explanatory bodies and tests for their respective changes.

- **P3 — Repository-rule violation: required release and API documentation is absent.** [CONTRIBUTING.md:24](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/CONTRIBUTING.md:24) requires notable bug fixes and changed behavior in `CHANGELOG.md`, with functional changes also documented in godoc. This PR changes malformed-payload handling and returned errors but changes neither artifact. The frozen description states no exception.

## Spec

- **P2 — Unmet hardening scope: zero-dimensional nested elements retain substantial allocation before rejection.** [marshal.go:1142](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal.go:1142) permits `vector<vector<float,0>,N>` with N equal to its nonempty payload length. Into `[][]float32`, the decoder allocates **24N bytes on amd64** before the first inner vector rejects its nonempty chunk: a 1 MiB payload causes 24 MiB of outer slice-header allocation. This exposure predates the PR; it remains unclosed by the advertised recursive hardening. The description’s companion `dim < 1` rejection is absent from both pinned parsers. The new allocation test exercises inner dimension three instead.

- **P3 — Factual documentation defect: the universal regression-test claim is false.** The frozen description says “Every new test fails against pristine `marshal.go`/`helpers.go`.” The compatibility test at [marshal_vector_test.go:937](/tmp/review-bench-codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17-CMsmSG/tidepool/marshal_vector_test.go:937) succeeds through unchanged base branches for both nil and empty payloads. The exact-size float acceptance test also succeeds at base. These are legitimate compatibility tests; the reproduction claim is inaccurate.

All three files and both commits were reviewed independently. No tests, builds, or external checks were run; CI claims, linked issue contents, and 32-bit execution remain unverified. HEAD and the clean working tree are unchanged.

  "body": "`unmarshalVector` runs on the goroutine that called `Scan`, where nothing recovers — the
driver's only `recover()` is `parseFrame`'s. Two inputs a server can send end the process
there.

**Scope**

In:

- `info.Dimensions` is the peer's number and reaches `make` and `reflect.MakeSlice`
  unbounded. The fast paths' `len(data) == Dimensions*8` check does not bound it: a
  dimension of `1<<61 + 1` wraps that product to exactly 8, so an 8-byte value passes and
  the allocation dies. The bound now sits ahead of every consumer, dividing by
  `vectorElemMinSize` — recursive, because `vectorFixedElemSize` returns 0 for a nested
  vector, exactly the element type whose real minimum is largest. Measured on
  `vector<vector<float,3>,N>`: 24 bytes allocated per payload byte before, 3.5 KB flat now.
- `reflect.TypeOf(info.Zero())` is nil whenever the element type has no Go type, and
  `.Kind()` dereferences it. Two **well-formed** column types reach it: a nested vector,
  whose inner type resolves from the bare `...VectorType` prefix, and any element type this
  driver does not know. `getCassandraLongType` now keeps that name so the error can say
  which type the server sent.

**Behaviour change**: a short or zero-length non-NULL payload used to decode to zero values
— `vector<int,3>` over an empty payload gave `[0 0 0], nil` — and now errors. That was
silent corruption. The bound's message also replaces the fast paths' exact byte count
("expected 24 bytes, got 16") when it fires first.

Out — making a nested vector actually decode into `interface{}`, which now errors rather
than crashing: #1085. Out — surplus trailing bytes, left exactly as found: #1086. Out — a
variable-length element's vint length narrowing to a negative and decoding to empty with a
nil error, which this bound does not catch: #1106.

Lands with #1093, which rejects `dim < 1` in the metadata parsers.

Verified with `make check` and `make test-unit`. Every new test fails against pristine
`marshal.go`/`helpers.go` — `reflect.MakeSlice: negative len`, `allocation size out of
range`, and two nil-pointer dereferences. Not covered: no live-node run.

      "messageBody": "unmarshalVector turned a peer-supplied dimension into an allocation
before it looked at the value: a negative count panicked in
reflect.MakeSlice, and a large positive one either panicked in makeslice
or exhausted the heap. Both land on the goroutine that called Scan,
where nothing recovers.

The bound sits ahead of the float fast paths because their
len(data) == Dimensions*8 check can be satisfied by a count large enough
for that product to wrap; once it is there, the multiplication cannot
overflow. Every element takes at least one byte on the wire, so a count
the buffer cannot hold is rejected the way unmarshalList already does.
